title: Database access with database/sql and pgx

videos.script: Stop boxoffice, start it again, and every sale is gone. This lesson gives it a memory. {{install}} First a PostgreSQL of your own. Two commands from Ubuntu's archive, one role, one database. And the four ways a connection fails, each with its message. {{schema}} Then the table. The rules the store enforced in Go move into the database, where no bug can get around them. {{sql}} Go talks to it two ways. database/sql is the standard interface, and its DB is a pool, not a connection. pgx is PostgreSQL's own client, and boxoffice uses it. {{quote}} An apostrophe in an event's name shows why a value never goes inside the SQL text. {{errors}} Then the three things that come back that are not rows. A NULL, a missing row, and a rule the database refused to break. {{run}} At the end, you restart the server, and this time the sales are still there.
